title: The Aquifer That Moved 1,500 ft³/day, Not 72,000
featured_title: THE AQUIFER THAT MOVED 1500 CUBIC FEET PER DAY NOT 72000
subject: civil

presentation.challenge: The hydraulic gradient was correct, but the plan-view area was used instead of the area perpendicular to groundwater flow. The aquifer moved 1,500 ft³/day.

practice.primary_question: How are hydraulic conductivity, hydraulic gradient, and cross-sectional flow area combined using Darcy's law for a confined aquifer?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Using plan-view aquifer area instead of the cross-sectional area normal to groundwater flow.

case_dna.target_misconception: Darcy flow uses aquifer length times width as the flow area.
case_dna.why_plausible: Length and width define the visible aquifer footprint, but Darcy's area is normal to the direction of flow.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: For K=30 ft/day, Δh=6 ft over L=1200 ft, thickness=25 ft, and width=400 ft, i=0.005 and A=10,000 ft², giving Q=1,500 ft³/day.
case_dna.corrected_model: Use Q=KiA with A equal to saturated thickness times width for horizontal confined flow.

problem_statement: A confined aquifer has hydraulic conductivity K=30 ft/day, saturated thickness b=25 ft, and width perpendicular to flow W=400 ft. Hydraulic head drops 6 ft over a flow length of 1,200 ft. Determine discharge using Darcy's law Q=KiA.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The aquifer footprint was mistaken for the groundwater flow area.
gates.prompt: Which dimensions form the area normal to horizontal flow?

options.label: Q=Ki(bW)
options.reason: Darcy area is perpendicular to the flow direction.

options.label: Q=Ki(LW)
options.reason: L×W is plan area, not the cross section normal to flow.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove Darcy discharge
gates.hint: The 1,200-ft length belongs in the hydraulic gradient, not the flow area.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: Flow area must be perpendicular to groundwater motion

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: The plan-view footprint arithmetic is correct.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: Darcy's law requires area normal to flow, not plan-view footprint.

evidence_choices.label: A=25×400=10,000 ft² and Q=1,500 ft³/day
evidence_choices.reason: This uses the correct cross-sectional flow area.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Limit groundwater flow to 1,000 ft³/day
gates.constraint: Keep geometry and head gradient unchanged.

options.label: Hydraulic conductivity must be 20 ft/day or less

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply Darcy's law again
gates.prompt: K=20 ft/day, b=30 ft, W=300 ft, Δh=9 ft, L=1500 ft. What is Q?

options.label: 5,400 ft³/day
options.reason: That does not use the stated gradient and normal area correctly.

gates.explanation: Darcy flow is hydraulic conductivity times hydraulic gradient times normal flow area.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the groundwater calculation
gates.confirmation: I confirm that Darcy's law uses the cross-sectional area normal to flow, not the aquifer plan area.

items.label: What failed
items.value: Plan area was used as Darcy flow area.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: Flow area must be normal to the groundwater direction.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Use Q=KiA with i=Δh/L and A=bW for the stated confined aquifer.

faqs.q: What area is used in Darcy's law for horizontal confined flow?
faqs.a: The saturated thickness times width, normal to the flow direction.
